clue.text: Iberian leaders in terrible tirade such as this

definitions.text: Iberian leaders in terrible tirade such as this

indicators.note: in places the leading letters inside the jumbled word tirade
a terrible tirade is a badly mangled one, so its letters are jumbled
the leaders of Iberian are its opening letters, here the first two

explanation.surface: A ranting speech, perhaps against Spain, delivered by Iberian chiefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' makes DIATRE from TIRADE; 'in' puts IB, the first two letters of Iberian ('leaders'), inside it. The whole clue also describes the answer: a terrible tirade such as this.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter, violent verbal attack is exactly the kind of speech the clue describes.

clue.text: Pit overseer with record in business performance

indicators.note: in puts the record inside the word for business performance

parts.note: duty is the performance of one's business or obligation
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A mine manager has a strong record of doing business.
explanation.walkthrough: A deputy is a coal-mining official responsible for safety in a district of the pit.
explanation.definitionFit: In British coal mines this official supervised a section of the workings.

clue.text: Farthest point reached by a Continental river-horse

parts.note: the Po is a river of Italy, on the European Continent
gee, or gee-gee, is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: The furthest a European hippopotamus has travelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river-horse' suggests a hippopotamus, but it splits into river (PO) and horse (GEE).
explanation.definitionFit: An apogee is the highest or most distant point, as in an orbit or a career.

clue.text: Make another introduction, as does 1 dn

explanation.surface: Someone introduces again, as a stand-in might.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 down is DEPUTY: a deputy stands in for, and so acts for, another.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyphenated, it means present again; whole, it means to act on behalf of someone, as a deputy does.

clue.text: Support Prom conductor's valet -though an uncouth fellow

parts.note: to back is to support
Sir Henry Wood founded and conducted the Proms, London's summer concert series
a manservant or valet is a man

explanation.surface: Backing the Proms conductor's servant, though he is rough-mannered.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are London's long-running summer classical concerts, which Henry Wood conducted for decades; 'though' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A backwoodsman lives in remote country and is thought of as rough or unsophisticated.

clue.text: A comment to take notice of

explanation.surface: Someone advises paying attention to a particular comment.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is an observation or comment; as a verb it means to observe or notice.

clue.text: Change due under the Spanish dodge

indicators.note: under means in this down entry the jumbled letters come below the article

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: change asks for the letters of due to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Under Spanish rules, a bill may be altered to avoid paying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' turns DUE into UDE; 'under' places it beneath EL in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude is to evade or escape, much as one dodges a blow.

clue.text: Fare suitable for the theatre gallery?

definitions.text: Fare suitable for the theatre gallery?

parts.words: Fare suitable for the theatre gallery?
parts.note: the highest seats in a theatre are called the gods, so food fit for the gods is meant

explanation.surface: Wondering what snacks to sell in the cheap seats upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The top gallery of a theatre is nicknamed 'the gods', so food for them is the food of the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this was the food of the gods, conferring immortality.

clue.text: Irish scene of flying fur

parts.note: a town in Ireland whose legendary cats fought until only their tails remained

explanation.surface: A fierce brawl breaks out somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kilkenny cats of the rhyme fought so fiercely that they ate each other; 'flying fur' is a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: This Irish town and county is famous for the proverbial cats that fought to the death.

clue.text: Expectation of a probable customer

explanation.surface: A salesman hopes that a likely buyer will come through.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a likely future outcome, and also a potential client a salesman hopes to win.

clue.text: Two first-class shots, they say, secured this Asian bird

indicators.note: they say tells us the letters come from how the shots are spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a bull, or bullseye, is a first-class shot at a target; two of them give the sounds

explanation.surface: A marksman bags an exotic bird with a couple of excellent shots.
explanation.walkthrough: A bull is the bullseye in darts or shooting; said twice it sounds like the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulbul is a songbird of Asia and Africa, a kind of thrush-like passerine.

clue.text: Ability to respond positively when organized vice is sensed

indicators.note: organized means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Responding firmly once organized crime has been detected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organized' rearranges the twelve letters of VICE IS SENSED; 'when' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being firm and quick to make up one's mind is the quality described.

clue.text: Subject that takes the stuffing out of most he-men

indicators.note: stuffing is what lies inside, so taking it out means extracting letters from within these words

explanation.surface: Something deflates the macho bravado of most muscular men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the stuffing out of' points to the letters inside 'most he-men', running across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic or subject of a discussion, essay or piece of music.

clue.text: Looking dismal we plead for one outside Ohio

indicators.note: outside means the word we wraps around the state's abbreviation

parts.note: O is a postal-style abbreviation for the US state Ohio
to plead is to beg
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people look miserable as they ask for one person waiting beyond Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts WE around O to make WOE, then BEG and ONE follow; 'for' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Woebegone describes a sad, miserable appearance.

clue.text: Maybe Jack's rank in the Church?

definitions.text: Maybe Jack's rank in the Church?

parts.words: Maybe Jack's rank in the Church?
parts.note: a playing card's value, such as a knave's, is one sense; a religious body such as the Methodists is the other

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what position a man called Jack holds in the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack looks like a churchman's name, but it is the playing card; its face value and a branch of the Church share one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the face value of a card or banknote and a distinct religious grouping.

clue.text: Security device for those at sea

definitions.text: Security device for those at sea

parts.words: Security device for those at sea
parts.note: a place or fixing where vessels can be held fast, read as a safety gadget

explanation.surface: A safety device for sailors, perhaps a lifejacket.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a gadget, but the security is a ship being held steady in harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorage is a place where ships may anchor, and also the hold an anchor gives.

clue.text: Gift of iron hoop

parts.note: taken as written
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a hoop is a ring

explanation.surface: A present consisting of an iron hoop.
explanation.definitionFit: An offering is something given, especially as a present or sacrifice.

clue.text: Cetacean loses nothing from deficient equilibrium

indicators.note: loses means one letter is dropped from the word for deficient

parts.note: poor means deficient or lacking
O looks like zero, nothing
poise is balance or equilibrium

explanation.surface: A whale-like creature gets nothing from its poor sense of balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' drops an O from POOR to give POR, which precedes POISE; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A porpoise is a small toothed whale, one of the cetaceans.

clue.text: 21, possibly, is part of the illustration

parts.note: the answer to 21 across is a seafront promenade, an example of a front
taken as written
a part is a piece

explanation.surface: A seaside walk may form part of a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 across is ESPLANADE, a seaside promenade, which the British also call the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontispiece is the illustration facing a book's title page.

clue.text: Musicians set about former Head of Television

indicators.note: about means the word set is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
ex means former

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of Television

explanation.surface: Performers take on a one-time television chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SET around EX and T, splitting it as S...ET.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextet is a group of six players or singers.

clue.text: Mustachioed type ate oysters with chips perhaps

definitions.text: Mustachioed type ate oysters with chips perhaps

parts.words: Mustachioed type ate oysters with chips perhaps
parts.note: the tusked beast of Lewis Carroll's poem who dined on oysters with the Carpenter, Chips being a carpenter's nickname

explanation.surface: A man with a moustache had oysters and chips.
explanation.walkthrough: Chips is a traditional nickname for a carpenter; in Lewis Carroll's poem the Walrus and the Carpenter eat the oysters.
explanation.definitionFit: This whiskered sea mammal is the oyster-eater of Carroll's poem, and gives its name to a drooping moustache.

clue.text: Design advertisement found among directions for the walk

indicators.note: found among means the other pieces sit inside the compass letters

parts.note: E, S and E are compass directions (east, south, east)
a design is a plan

explanation.surface: A promotional design turns up among signposts for a footpath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found among' splits E, S, E so that PLAN and AD sit between S and the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a long level promenade for walking, often along a seafront.

clue.text: Strong man in position of cobbler, almost

parts.note: at means in position, as in at home

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a last is the foot-shaped block a cobbler works on

explanation.surface: A muscular man stands where the shoemaker usually does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the T of LAST, the cobbler's foot-shaped block; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlas is the Titan of Greek myth who held up the heavens, a byword for strength.

clue.text: Last character to get an honour, years back

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

indicators.note: back means the word for years is written from right to left

parts.note: an age is a long period of years

explanation.surface: Someone finally receives an award after many years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns AGE into EGA, which follows OM; 'to get' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: A product of the freeze? It depends

definitions.text: A product of the freeze? It depends

parts.words: A product of the freeze? It depends
parts.note: something formed by frost that hangs down, depend meaning hang in its old sense

explanation.surface: A hedging reply to a question about the results of a cold snap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It depends' sounds like a non-committal answer, but depend literally means hang down, which this frozen spike does.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging spike of ice forms when dripping water freezes.

clue.text: One who absconds — gone with the wind, presumably

explanation.surface: A runaway vanishes as if blown away.
explanation.definitionFit: A levanter is someone who runs off to dodge debts, and also a strong easterly wind in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Perhaps 'e sings a sort of rock

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A Cockney fellow may be singing some type of rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'e sings is Cockney for 'he sings'; 'Perhaps' rearranges its six letters, and rock is stone, not music.
explanation.definitionFit: Gneiss is a coarse-grained banded metamorphic stone.

clue.text: A distress signal about most effective fire protection

indicators.note: about means the distress call goes around the other word

parts.note: SOS is the Morse distress signal
best means most effective

explanation.surface: A call for help is the best way to deal with a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SOS around BEST, giving SBESTOS after A.
explanation.definitionFit: This fibrous mineral was long used in fireproof materials.
